blocks.content: The primary objective of establishing Special Courts is to ensure speedy justice and reduce the pendency of specialized cases in the regular judicial system.

rows: Subject-specific statutes (e.g., POCSO, NIA, SC/ST Act)
Strict adherence to CPC and CrPC rules
Simplified, summary trials subject to strict timeframes
Fast-track clearance of specific specialized cases

items: Gram Nyayalayas exercise both civil and criminal jurisdiction and are guided by the principles of natural justice rather than rigid procedure rules.
Establishment of Family Courts is compulsory in every city or town with a population exceeding 10 lakhs (1 million).
An appeal against any judgment or order of an NIA Special Court lies directly to the High Court both on facts and on law.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Special Courts are created under specific statutory mandates to expedite trials for designated categories of offenses.
Gram Nyayalayas function as mobile courts aimed at delivering affordable and speedy justice at the doorstep of rural citizens.
Family Courts mandate conciliation and informal procedures to settle matrimonial and domestic disputes peacefully.
Fast Track Special Courts (FTSCs) specifically target sexual offenses under the IPC and the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act.
Judges of Special Courts under central statutes like the NIA Act are designated in consultation with the respective High Court.
